segments.title: Chương 40: 0040
segments.content:
Feng Tao stared at the feedback and said, "Total downloads have already exceeded 3100. Zone 1 is lagging so badly it's unplayable, and Zone 2 is under a lot of pressure too. A lot of players from Zone 1 are heading straight for Zone 5. I guess they've figured out that Zone 5 is the smoothest..."

Yang Yuhui, on the other hand, said, "I'm chatting with some net cafe managers. One of them said that four or five players at his cafe had arranged to play our private server together. As they were playing, they attracted the people next to them who were playing the official version. Now there are seventeen or eighteen people playing Abyss Legend in his net cafe!"

"How many more people can Zones 3, 4, and 5 hold?" Tao Chenggang asked.

Feng Tao said, "In just these few minutes, Zone 5 is almost full too. It's probably players from Zone 1 who switched over because of the lag. Zones 3 and 4 are still relatively smooth, but together they can only hold another four or five hundred people. And the download count is still climbing!"

Tao Chenggang commanded, "Contact the major private server forums and take down the download links immediately!"

17173 hadn't provided an official download link. After all, it was a legitimate portal website and couldn't openly offer download services for a private server.

Moreover, in late 2003, you couldn't embed hyperlinks or attachments in posts and replies.

The download links for Abyss Legend were posted on private server forums like 17577, 7GG, and Ledu, and Tao Chenggang had paid them all for promotion.

Just as Yang Yuhui was contacting the forums to take down the links, Chen Guiliang was furiously typing up a post:

"Wuwuwuwu, I'm going to cry my eyes out. Why are there so many players? The Little Tyrant server I rented isn't enough."

"Good heavens, you guys are too awesome. Brothers and sisters, I'm so sorry, but we have to turn off the downloads for today, or else the game will be unplayable!"

Immediately after, Chen Guiliang switched to a bystander account and replied in the game's update log: "Who was it that just said a server for 5,000 people would be more than enough? And that he's so damn awesome. Awesome my ass!"

He copied the content and sent it to the head of the water army, adding a few more words, "Everyone below, keep the formation": "Don't say anything else, just copy and paste this reply!"

Soon, the thread was flooded with a stream of replies, instantly shooting up twenty or thirty floors: "With such a huge server capacity, it must be more than enough. I'm so damn awesome! Everyone below, keep the formation."

Feng Tao shouted, "It's lagging! Zone 2 and Zone 5 are totally lagging, and Zones 3 and 4 are almost full too."

"Didn't we take down the download links?" Tao Chenggang asked.

Feng Tao said, "While Yangyu was contacting the forums to take down the links, the download count shot up by another 400 plus. They must have already been downloading and just finished. And those net cafes, they download it once and can install it on dozens of computers. The actual number of players is definitely much higher than the download count!"

Chen Guiliang comforted him, "It's fine. A lot of netizens are just here for the excitement, and some are playing private servers to get back at Shanda. They'll be leaving in a little while."

As they spoke, all five zones became full.

Xie Yang had been staring at the forums and yelled anxiously, "A lot of netizens have started cursing."

Feng Tao said, "They're cursing in the game too."

Chen Guiliang glanced at a few replies on the forum and found that those cursing about the game being too laggy weren't being particularly harsh. Some were even taking pleasure in the misfortune.

The ones really spewing vitriol were the netizens who couldn't download and hadn't even gotten into the game yet.

You could put yourself in their shoes: you get home from work on a Friday, excitedly downloading a game. Your internet speed is deathly slow. You finally get to 99%, and suddenly the download link is cut off...

Wouldn't you start cursing?

Chen Guiliang quickly commanded, "In those two hot threads, keep switching accounts and copy-pasting the reply from before. Don't get into flame wars with the netizens, just drown them out with a uniform reply! Also, post an in-game announcement to apologize, explain the reason in detail, and invite them to chat on the forums."

Xie Yang and the other water army members immediately got to work.

Before long, Xie Yang was surprised to find that the tide of public opinion had actually turned.

The netizens' initial complaints and curses gradually turned into mostly teasing and ridicule, and they even started copying and pasting the phrase: "Haha, with such a huge server capacity, it must be more than enough. I'm so damn awesome! Everyone below, keep the formation."

There were even a few little tricksters intentionally causing trouble: "Hey, I'm just here to break the formation. Come and get me, come get me through the internet cable."

Xie Yang was utterly shocked and asked, "Brother Chen, did you anticipate this situation, which is why you posted that self-aggrandizing thread in advance? And then had us quote the self-aggrandizing content to steer player opinion towards irony and ridicule?"

Hearing this, everyone else also looked at Chen Guiliang.

Chen Guiliang explained, "Cursing at a game is different from cursing at a person. I posted in advance in my capacity as the private server operator, and deliberately boasted to leave a handle for criticism. It was to give the netizens a target to vent their anger on, to shift their focus, and to give them a way to back down. Especially for those netizens who had downloaded over 50% but were suddenly unable to continue, they're extremely furious right now."

Tao Chenggang understood at once, "Guide the netizens from cursing the game to cursing the person running the game. And this person has been acting like a brother to the netizens all along, even deliberately boasting like a clown. It's like when a good friend messes things up, and messes them up in a particularly ridiculous and comical way. At that point, you can switch from cursing to teasing and mocking. After the teasing and mocking is done, you're still friends!"

"Right," Chen Guiliang said, "These netizens were already leaning our way because of the posts from the past few days. Most of them didn't actually start cursing directly. Their anger is only temporary. As long as we don't provoke them further, a little trick like this is enough to divert their attention."

Chen Guiliang added, "Besides, it can also give them a sense of vanity. It makes them feel that the game lagging and the downloads being cut off isn't because we did something wrong, but because their own power is too great. They'll feel like they're the awesome ones for being able to crash a private server."

"Amazing!"

Xie Yang was filled with admiration. He felt like he had learned something new again.

Yang Yuhui exclaimed in amazement, "Dude, how does your brain work?"

Feng Tao laughed heartily, "He's my nephew, smart like me."

The others in the room also chimed in with exclamations of "awesome."

Tao Xue hadn't understood anything about private servers and had no interest in games.

She had been wandering around the room bored, but now hearing everyone praise Chen Guiliang, Tao Xue inexplicably felt that he was incredibly capable.

Chen Guiliang was still replying to posts: "Wuwuwuwu, go ahead and curse me. I was so silly and naive. I thought a 5,000-person server would be enough, I didn't expect you brothers and sisters to be so awesome. I've already rented a new server, we can open a new zone tomorrow! How many people came to play tonight? You've overloaded the Little Tyrant server. Do you have to be so damn awesome?"

Chen Guiliang switched accounts again and replied: "I'm so damn awesome, the server is more than enough. Keep the formation."

He then sent a message to the water army on QQ: "Quick, copy this line and keep replying! The previous one was too long. Now that the netizens are familiar with it, switch to this shorter one."

Tao Chenggang pondered the changing length of the replies and looked at the composed Chen Guiliang giving commands, thinking with amazement: This kid is a natural-born leader!

Chen Guiliang was still reading the threads and noticed many people replying "Little Tyrant server, laughing my ass off."

He immediately realized this meme didn't exist yet and instructed the water army, "Quick, start spamming: Little Tyrant server, laughing my ass off. Keep the formation!"

Then, Chen Guiliang looked back at his own post and had the water army make a meme out of the "so silly and naive" phrase he had used.

At this time, the "keep the formation" style of posting wasn't yet popular on forums.

Under the guidance of the water army, the netizens found it really interesting.

For a time, the major game forums became lively and full of laughter, with netizens getting endless enjoyment out of the memes.

Chen Guiliang then, in the guise of a netizen whose download was cut off, guided similar players to completely change their mindset and emotions. That is, the power of us netizens is immense, we scared the private server into not even daring to keep the links up!

Those who couldn't stand the laggy servers, and those who couldn't download the game, all started playing the post-piling game.

As far as the eye could see, all the replies were "keep the formation."

It seemed that building up posts and spamming like this was even more fun than playing the game itself.

Tianya Forum.

A post appeared: Private server blunder, the Little Tyrant server is making me laugh my ass off.

"I just got home from work and turned on my computer to download Abyss Legend. Don't even get me started on the download speed. I finally got to 42%, and then it suddenly said I couldn't continue downloading. I went to the forums to check, and a lot of people were cursing. The download links have been cut off."

"Then I looked at the threads. I was originally planning to curse them out, but I ended up laughing my head off. The guy who set up this private server claimed it could hold 5,000 people, even said it was more than enough and that he was super awesome. The servers are totally overloaded, and now the guy is getting cursed out so bad he doesn't dare show his face. The threads are all a uniform 'keep the formation.'"

"Oh right, he also said he was so silly and naive, and that he rented a Little Tyrant server. Little Tyrant is such a perfect description..."

"The netizens on the game forums are all witty geniuses, the more I read, the more I want to laugh... Here's the link, let's all go join the fun."

In an era where people could spend all night in chat rooms without feeling tired, where you could chat with a stranger on QQ for a whole day, even a slightly interesting event could easily attract a large crowd of onlookers.

Before long, follow-up posts appeared on the game forums.

"Tianya netizen was here. I'm so damn awesome, keep the formation."

"Xici Hutong netizen was here. I'm so damn awesome, keep the formation."

"Shuimu Tsinghua BBS netizen was here. I'm so damn awesome, keep the formation."

"Mop netizen..."

These guys were definitely not brought in by the water army!

Many of them had never even played an online game before and were purely there to check in and join the excitement.

This server overload crisis, under Chen Guiliang's deliberate guidance, had already turned into a so-called blunder.

Moreover, it directly created four hot memes: "I'm so damn awesome," "keep the formation," "so silly and naive," and "Little Tyrant server."

The staff on duty at 17173 noticed a sharp increase in website traffic and quickly called their supervisor to capitalize on the opportunity and expand their influence.

They didn't care what Shanda would think, nor did they care about the fate of Abyss Legend. That very night, they rushed out an article and put it on the homepage: Private Server Blunder Attracts Eager Onlookers from Across the Nation.

After this news article was posted on the homepage, many netizens who didn't play private servers also came to check out the threads out of curiosity.

The more they read, the more interesting they found it, so they simply stayed on the forums to spam and play with the memes. Many even decided to wait for the downloads to be restored so they could go check out what this Abyss Legend private server was like.

And on major forums and university BBSes, in threads unrelated to games, "I'm so damn awesome" and "keep the formation" started to appear.

Netizens who were oblivious to all this were completely baffled and quickly asked what was going on.

It was still spreading!

It even spread into the real world.

Popular Computer Software magazine was conducting related research and statistics to publish the 2003 China Computer Game Industry Report on New Year's Day next year.

Data from game companies and sales outlets wouldn't be available until the end of December.

But they had already started interviewing industry professionals and players. One part of this involved interviewing active users on game forums, and they even collaborated with 17173 to create a survey.

Editor Lao Wei was in charge of interviewing online game users, and the evenings on weekends were the most convenient time to act.

He had only been browsing the website for a short while when he saw those hot threads. He quickly inquired about the whole story and then rapidly skimmed through the posts and replies.

Lao Wei's eyes lit up as he read. He believed he could write an article to report on this, and he had even conceptualized the content.

It would be about two Legend players who loved the game. Out of nostalgia for the game and their old friends, they decided to make their own private server after getting drunk. They announced their idea on a forum, which resonated with a large number of netizens, ultimately leading to a series of comical events. Moreover, it created a bunch of popular terms like "game refugees," "internet orphans," "Little Tyrant server," "I'm so damn awesome," "keep the formation," and "so silly and naive."

Of course, he would also have to discuss the legality of private servers and call on relevant authorities to improve the laws, which would add depth to the report.

This kind of magazine article was popular with many readers.

Because countless people across the country couldn't be online every day.

Some magazines could even keep readers engrossed by simply copying and pasting forum threads.

Chen Guiliang looked at the news article on the 17173 homepage, remained silent for a long while, and said, "Brother Gang, let's just wait for the lawyer's letter or a call from Shanda."

Tao Chenggang was chain-smoking Huazis, unsure whether to be happy or worried. "What do you think Shanda will do?"

"Who knows?" Chen Guiliang said.

Feng Tao suddenly shouted from the side, "The zones aren't lagging much anymore. It's probably the netizens who were just here for the show who have already left the game. And some people, after disconnecting, just went to the forums to pile up posts instead."

Yang Yuhui then said, "Brother Gang, an editor from Popular Computer Software added me on QQ. He says he wants to interview us."

Tao Chenggang: "..."

Chen Guiliang: "..."

They had no idea yet that the private server community had already been ignited.

At this very moment, all their peers who ran private servers were paying close attention to Abyss Legend.

They had no choice but to pay attention. The topic was generating too much buzz, and it's not like they were blind.
